differential: Molluscum contagiosum
Skin-colored umbilicated papules with central dimpling are pathognomonic for molluscum contagiosum, which is common in HIV patients with immunosuppression.
Cryptococcosis (cutaneous)
HIV patients can develop disseminated cryptococcosis with umbilicated skin lesions resembling molluscum, and cervical lymphadenopathy supports systemic infection.
Disseminated histoplasmosis
This can present with umbilicated papules in immunocompromised HIV patients and cause lymphadenopathy, though less common than molluscum.
Basal cell carcinoma (multiple)
Multiple skin-colored papules on sun-exposed areas could represent basal cell carcinomas, though the dimpled center and distribution make this less likely.
Penicilliosis (Talaromyces marneffei)
This endemic mycosis in HIV patients presents with umbilicated papules resembling molluscum and causes lymphadenopathy, though more common in Southeast Asia.
